questions.subject: भूगोल

questions.explanation: जनसंख्या, शहरीकरण र आर्थिक गतिविधि बढ्दा पानी, भूमि, ऊर्जा तथा अन्य स्रोतको माग र व्यवस्थापन चुनौती बदलिन सक्छ।

समुद्री मार्गको अवस्थिति राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षासँग कहिल्यै जोडिँदैन

questions.explanation: महत्वपूर्ण जलडमरूमध्य, नहर र समुद्री मार्ग विश्व व्यापार तथा रणनीतिक सुरक्षाका दृष्टिले महत्वपूर्ण हुन सक्छन्।

questions.category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
questions.question: Statement: The school should provide a digital copy of the timetable to parents. Assumptions: I. Parents may need convenient access to the timetable. II. Every parent owns a smartphone.
questions.solution: Convenient access is a reasonable implicit basis. Universal smartphone ownership is not required by the recommendation.

questions.category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
questions.question: All effective projects have measurable objectives. Some government projects are effective. No project with unclear objectives is measurable. Which conclusion must be true?
options: No government project has unclear objectives
Some government projects have measurable objectives
questions.solution: The effective government projects have measurable objectives by the first statement.

questions.category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
questions.question: Statements: All permits are documents. No document is confidential. Conclusions: I. No permit is confidential. II. Some documents are permits.
questions.solution: Every permit is a document and no document is confidential, so no permit is confidential. Existence of permits is not stated.

questions.category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
questions.question: Statements: All auditors are analysts. Some analysts are planners. Conclusions: I. Some auditors are planners. II. All auditors are analysts.
questions.solution: Conclusion II directly restates the first statement. Conclusion I does not necessarily follow because the analysts who are planners need not be auditors.

questions.category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
questions.question: Statement: A pilot program in three districts reduced average document-processing time by 18%, while staffing levels remained unchanged. Conclusions: I. The pilot may have improved process efficiency. II. The same 18% reduction will necessarily occur everywhere.
questions.solution: The observed result supports a possible efficiency improvement. It cannot guarantee an identical result elsewhere.

questions.category: General Mental Ability, Logical & Analytical Ability
questions.question: Four interviews P, Q, R and S are scheduled in four slots. Q is before R. S is immediately after P. R is not last. Which sequence is valid?
questions.solution: Q-P-S-R satisfies Q before R, S immediately after P, and R is last—so it violates R not last. Therefore none? Check options: P-S-Q-R also has R last; P-Q-S-R has R last; S-P-Q-R has S not after P. Hence no sequence is valid.

questions.passage: One scientific study rarely settles a complex question. Replication, comparison with other evidence and careful interpretation increase confidence. Good science communication requires both accuracy and clarity.
questions.question: Which inference is most reasonable?
questions.solution: Careful interpretation and accurate communication imply honest treatment of uncertainty.

questions.passage: Public trust depends on fair procedures, evidence and accountability. Transparency helps citizens evaluate performance and makes mistakes easier to identify and correct. Trust does not require agreement with every decision.
questions.question: Which statement is FALSE?

questions.solution: The passage says trust does not require agreement with every decision.

questions.passage: Forests provide timber as well as carbon storage, water regulation, soil protection and habitat. Some benefits are shared without direct payment, so private incentives may differ from wider social benefits.
questions.question: Conservation policy should
questions.solution: Policy should consider both private incentives and social benefits.

questions.passage: Energy efficiency can reduce resource use without reducing services. Insulation, efficient appliances and sensible operating practices can cut waste. Small improvements can have a large combined effect across many buildings.
questions.question: Why can small improvements matter?
options: Their combined effect can be substantial
questions.solution: Many small improvements can add up to substantial savings.

questions.passage: Public trust depends on fair procedures, evidence and accountability. Transparency helps citizens evaluate performance and makes mistakes easier to identify and correct. Trust does not require agreement with every decision.
questions.question: Transparency helps citizens
questions.solution: Publishing information helps citizens evaluate performance.

questions.question: Choose the correct noun form of “resilient”.
questions.solution: “resilience” is the correct derived form required by the sentence.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to “prudent”.
questions.solution: “cautious” is the closest synonym in this context.

questions.question: In “The issue remains contentious,” what does “contentious” mean?
questions.solution: The context indicates that “likely to cause disagreement” is the intended meaning.

questions.question: Choose the correct noun form of “efficient”.
questions.solution: “efficiency” is the correct derived form required by the sentence.

questions.question: Choose the correct adjective form of “industry” in “an _____ process”.
questions.solution: “industrial” is the correct derived form required by the sentence.

questions.question: In “The new evidence casts doubt on the claim,” what does “casts doubt on” mean?
questions.solution: The context indicates that “makes the claim less certain” is the intended meaning.

questions.question: In “The reform is likely to alleviate congestion,” what does “alleviate” mean?
questions.solution: The context indicates that “reduce the severity of” is the intended meaning.

questions.question: The reason ___ the project was delayed was lack of funding.
questions.solution: The standard construction is the reason why something happened.

questions.question: Choose the sentence closest in meaning: 'As soon as the bell rang, the students left.'
options: The students left long before the bell rang.
The students left although the bell never rang.
The students waited until after the bell rang.
No sooner had the bell rung than the students left.
questions.solution: No sooner had...than expresses an immediate sequence.

questions.question: If the data ___ more reliable, the conclusion would be stronger.
questions.solution: This hypothetical present condition uses were in the if-clause.

questions.question: I will call you when the meeting ___.
questions.solution: A future time clause introduced by when normally uses the present simple.

questions.question: Choose the best transformation: 'Despite being tired, she continued working.'
options: Although she tired, but she continued working.
Because she was tired, she stopped working.
Although she was tired, she continued working.
She continued working because she was tired.
questions.solution: Despite being tired can be expressed as Although she was tired.

questions.question: The programme seeks not only to train staff but also ___ systems.
questions.solution: Not only to train...but also to improve is parallel.

questions.question: By the time the guests arrived, we ___ dinner.
questions.solution: The earlier completed action takes the past perfect.

questions.question: She said that she ___ the document the following day.
questions.solution: In reported speech, will normally shifts to would when the reporting verb is past.
